deep.reconstruction:
Context (E477, Euler's 'Meditationes' on double sums, i.e. double zeta values). In §6 Euler writes the partial-fraction expansion of 1/(x^m (x+a)^n). The expansion has two finite rows:

(i) Σ_k (-1)^k C(n+k-1,k) a^{-(n+k)} x^{-(m-k)}
(ii) (-1)^m Σ_j C(m+j-1,j) a^{-(m+j)} (x+a)^{-(n-j)}

Each row stops when the exponent of x or of x+a reaches 1.

§7: sum over x = 1, 2, 3, ... Euler writes ∫1/z^λ for ζ(λ). He uses Σ_x (x+a)^{-λ} = ζ(λ) − H_a^{(λ)}, where H_a^{(λ)} = 1 + 2^{-λ} + ... + a^{-λ}. This gives

s(a) = Σ_x 1/(x^m (x+a)^n)
 = Σ_k (-1)^k C(n+k-1,k) ζ(m-k)/a^{n+k}
 + (-1)^m Σ_j C(m+j-1,j) [ζ(n-j) − H_a^{(n-j)}]/a^{m+j}.

The previous page has the first row. This page carries the ± rows with ζ(n-j) and the ∓ rows with H_a^{(n-j)}. Upper signs apply for m even, lower for m odd. Check with m = n = 1: 1/(x(x+a)) = (1/x − 1/(x+a))/a, so the sign is minus for m odd, as stated.

The ζ(1) terms come from k = m−1 in row (i) and j = n−1 in row (ii). They carry coefficients (-1)^{m-1}C(m+n-2,m-1)/a^{m+n-1} and (-1)^m C(m+n-2,n-1)/a^{m+n-1}, which cancel. So s(a) is a finite closed form in zeta values and finite harmonic sums of a.

§8: next sum over a = 1, 2, .... The first row becomes Σ_k (-1)^k C(n+k-1,k) ζ(n+k) ζ(m-k), as printed at the bottom of the page. The ± and ∓ rows continue overleaf as ζ(m+j)ζ(n-j) and Σ_a H_a^{(n-j)}/a^{m+j}. Euler writes the latter as ∫1/z^{m+j}(1/y^{n-j}); it is a double zeta (non-strict) sum.

Combining this with the m↔n counterpart (the 'right-hand' family of §5) expresses ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) through double sums with binomial coefficients. This is the classical Euler decomposition / evaluation scheme for double zeta values. The purpose is to evaluate double sums Σ H_a^{(n)}/a^m in terms of single zeta values.
errors: Printed typo in the last bracket: '1/2^{m-3}' should be 1/2^{n-3}. The closing parenthesis is also missing.

Euler's justification of finiteness ('both orders are continued only up to ∫1/z') is loose. The expression is finite because the two divergent ζ(1) = ∫1/z terms, one from each row, carry equal and opposite coefficients and cancel. When summing over a in §8, these paired terms must be dropped together; taken separately they would give divergent ζ(1)ζ(m+n-1) products.

ideas.what: Partial-fraction expansion of 1/(x^m (x+a)^n) summed over x, giving Σ_x 1/(x^m (x+a)^n) in terms of zeta values and partial sums H_a^{(k)}
ideas.modern_name: Partial-fraction (Euler) method for Tornheim/Mordell-type sums; shifted double zeta series
ideas.where_published: E477 itself, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Summing over a to express ζ(m)ζ(n) via binomially weighted double sums Σ H_a^{(k)}/a^l (Euler sums)
ideas.modern_name: Euler's decomposition formula for products of zeta values into double zeta values (shuffle/stuffle precursor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477); modern rediscussion by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995), Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst (1997), Zagier
ideas.where_published: E477; treated in Opera Omnia I.15 and in modern MZV literature

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known core computation of E477, Euler's double zeta paper. Its partial-fraction decomposition formula is widely cited and credited to Euler in the multiple zeta value literature. Nothing here is unknown.
